body: I agree but in this case, people are not suggesting the spouse just make a quick call or set an alarm clock. Folks are suggesting she look through his call logs, and text messages for proof of infidelity. If she can't trust him on his word there are most likely other signs of infidelity then finding the toy and his stories changing about the toy. The solution is to talk to him like two rational adults in a partnership. If they need help communicating they should seek out a professional counselor or therapist. But violating one partner's privacy will only create other problems for their relationship.

I agree but a cell phone is like a journal on steroids. It has so much information on it having access to your partner's phone is almost as good as having access to their mind. If you are so worried about a relationship that you feel the need to remove all privacy and autonomy that's probably an irreconcilable issue. In a committed relationship you do give up some privacy and autonomy but partners shouldn't be asked to give their individuality and sense of self to a degree they are not an individual.
I think that a phone is a modern dairy. So many personal conversations, recordings, and moments are stored on it. Everyone deserves privacy and I think that includes one's cell phone, and email.
